rationales: J.J. Thomson proposed a model of the atom, not the concept of electron orbits.
Rutherford proposed a nuclear model but did not introduce the concept of fixed orbits.
Planck developed quantum theory, not the atomic orbit concept.
Bohr introduced fixed orbits for electrons around the nucleus.
Mendeleev’s table was based mainly on atomic mass, not the modern long-form table.
The long-form periodic table is arranged on the basis of increasing atomic number.
Atomic mass is not the basis of the modern long-form periodic table.
Mass number is not the basis of the long-form periodic table.
Mass by mass percentage requires the masses of both solute and solution.
Mass by volume percentage requires solute mass per solution volume.
Volume by mass percentage expresses solute volume per solution mass, as in this example.
Volume by volume percentage requires the volumes of both solute and solution.
Metallic bonding involves attraction between metal ions and delocalized electrons, not electron transfer between atoms.
Electron transfer between atoms forms an ionic bond.
Covalent bonding forms by sharing electron pairs.
Coordinate covalent bonding forms when one atom donates both shared electrons.
A covalent bond pair does not consist of only one electron.
A bond pair usually consists of two shared electrons.
Three electrons do not make a covalent bond pair.
Four electrons are not a single bond pair.
Molecules with very low energy are unlikely to escape the liquid surface.
Moderate-energy molecules are less likely to escape than the highest-energy molecules.
The molecules that escape during evaporation have sufficiently high energy to overcome attractions at the surface.
This option is incorrect because the escaping molecules have high energy.
Sugar solution does not produce ions in water and is not an electrolyte.
Sulphuric acid solution produces ions and conducts electricity.
Lime solution contains ions and can conduct electricity.
Sodium chloride solution dissociates into ions and conducts electricity.
Some metals form ions with a single positive charge.
Some metals form ions with a double positive charge.
Some metals form ions with a triple positive charge.
Metals can form ions with all these positive charges.
A molecular formula gives the actual number of each type of atom in a molecule.
Formula mass is the sum of the atomic masses represented by a formula.
Chemical formula is a general representation and need not show the simplest ratio.
An empirical formula gives the simplest whole-number ratio of atoms in a compound.
Fluorine’s atomic number is not 5.
Fluorine’s atomic number is not 7.
Fluorine has 9 protons, so its atomic number is 9.
Fluorine’s atomic number is not 15.
The s subshell is not the subshell being filled in transition elements.
The p subshell is not the defining subshell being filled in transition elements.
The d subshell is being filled in transition elements.
The f subshell is filled in inner-transition elements, not the usual transition elements referred to here.
Size is too general and is not the specific term for half the internuclear distance.
Shielding effect describes the screening of nuclear charge by other electrons.
An orbit is a proposed path or region for an electron, not an atomic size measure.
Atomic radius is defined as half the distance between the nuclei of two bonded atoms of the same element.
An ionic bond forms through electron transfer rather than equal sharing.
A coordinate bond has both shared electrons donated by one atom.
A polar covalent bond involves unequal sharing of electrons.
A pure covalent bond involves equal sharing between similar atoms.
Lone is not the nature of Van der Waals forces.
Liquid describes a state of matter, not the nature of these forces.
Van der Waals forces are not chemical bonds in the usual sense.
Van der Waals forces are weak electrical attractions between particles.
Evaporation changes a liquid into a gas.
Melting changes a solid into a liquid.
Transpiration is water loss from plants, not gas changing into liquid.
Condensation is the change of a gas into a liquid.
